blogs.title: Rule 404(b) and the Intrinsic Evidence of Prior Firearm Possession: The 8th Circuit’s Verdict in Cutbank
blogs.description: This analysis dissects how the 8th Circuit upheld the admissibility of prior evidence that abetted the defendant’s possession of a sawed‑off rifle. It revisits the *Battle* precedent, clarifies the boundary between intrinsic and propensity evidence, and evaluates the court’s reasoning for the Confrontation Clause and hearsay issues. The piece discusses the practical flashpoint for defense counsel in firearms cases and the potential ripple effects on future rule‑404(b) disputes.

blogs.title: No Sentence Too High? The Cutbank Court Tackles ACMA’s Four‑Level Enhancement Under §2K2.1(b)(6)(B)
blogs.description: This post navigates the appellate court’s discussion of the Armed Career Criminal Act’s four‑level increase for "possession of a firearm in connection with another felony." The investigation clarifies how the district court applied the enhancement, how the guidelines range was correctly calculated, and how §3553(a)’s "necessary but not greater than necessary" principle was satisfied. The analysis also examines the effect of the "within‑range" standard on future sentencing determinations.

blogs.title: Harmless Error and Appellate Deference in Sentencing: The Cutbank Ruling as a Case Study
blogs.description: The article scrutinizes the court’s decision to let the District Court’s sentencing stand, foregrounding the harmless‑error doctrine, the "within‑range" analysis, and the deference standard enshrined in cases such as *Goodhouse* and *Masood*. It also outlines how the 8th Circuit required the district court to have correctly calculated the guideline range before it could look at §3553(a) factors, and the ramifications for correcting evidentiary and procedural errors on appeal.
